content: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitors, such as evolocumab, have demonstrated a significant impact on cholesterol management. In clinical trials, including GAUSS-1 and GAUSS-2, evolocumab was directly compared to ezetimibe, a commonly used cholesterol-lowering medication. The results of these studies showed that evolocumab achieved more substantial reductions in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels compared to ezetimibe. However, it was also observed that patients receiving evolocumab experienced slightly higher incidences of musculoskeletal adverse effects.
